I also really enjoy listening to people and helping my friends work through their problems. Reading up on why people behave the way they do is fascinating to me. But I don't enjoy having to support or counsel people all day. Persuading people or selling ideas really isn't my thing either.

Nothing satisfies me more than turning a messy spreadsheet into perfect order, with every record checked and every step of the process clearly laid out. I also really like leading a team and persuading people to back a plan, like when our CCA had to convince the school to approve a bigger budget. Working out why the numbers don't add up is genuinely fun for me too. On the other hand, hands-on work with tools, engines or wiring is something I really don't like.

What I don't like is routine admin like filing forms and keeping records. Helping people is where I want to be.

Running things is my favourite thing in the world; I chaired our faculty's orientation committee and negotiating with sponsors and getting everyone moving was amazing. I'm also really into keeping things organised, like building schedules, tracking budgets and making sure every detail is in place. Helping freshies settle in was kinda nice too. Hands-on work with tools or machines really isn't for me. I also dislike deep research or theory where you spend hours figuring out why something happens.

Honestly, I'd rather not spend my time helping other people.

I get a real kick out of leading a group project and convincing people to get behind an idea. I also enjoy planning things properly, keeping schedules and budgets neat and making sure every detail is in order. My dad runs a small workshop and I've spent most school holidays helping him with the machines, so I've always assumed I'd end up doing something hands-on like that. I'm not really into deep research or analysing data for hours. Creative stuff like drawing or designing also isn't my cup of tea.

And I strongly dislike tedious paperwork, like filling in forms and keeping records all day.

I love helping people and spending time with juniors who need someone to talk to. Creating things, like painting or designing, is one of the things I enjoy most. I also get curious about how things work and like reading up on them. I don't really enjoy artsy or creative work. I can't stand doing physical work with tools outdoors. Keeping detailed records and following strict procedures also drives me crazy.
